A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same epistemic GNN research, with matching architecture, proofs and original benchmarks despite retitling and reorganization. Their main texts, figures, tables and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on CLUTRR, GraphLog, RCC-8 and interval algebra, including ablations and message-passing sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds knowledge-graph completion experiments, efficiency measurements and expanded reasoning stress tests.

M1.justification: Matching FB to EpiGNN shows that the epistemic embeddings, composition function, pooling, facets and training objective are retained. The limited inference adaptation is tail-entity ranking for knowledge-graph completion using one pass of the existing forward-only model and candidate-entity scores (Appendix F.2).

E1.justification: v2 adds inductive tail prediction on four variants each of FB15k-237 and WN18RR. Appendix G.6 also extends RCC-8 and interval-algebra testing from at most 9 hops and 3 paths to 15 hops and 8 paths. Interval algebra itself already appeared in v1's Appendix A.6 and Table 13.

E2.justification: v2 adds Edge Transformers to the Graphlog comparison and CTP to the RCC-8/interval-algebra comparison. Its new KGC table introduces comparisons with Neural LP, DRUM, RuleN, GraIL, CoMPILE, TACT, SNRI, ConGLR and REST, alongside NBFNet; most comparator scores are explicitly sourced from prior papers.

E3.justification: The new KGC evaluation uses disjoint training/test graphs, Hits@10 with 50 negative samples and six message-passing rounds. Existing-setting documentation also changes: RCC-8 batch size rises from 64 to 128, and the margin search includes additional intermediate values (v1 Table 10/A.7.4; v2 Table 11/F.5). These reported revisions do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds parameter/runtime comparisons and substantially harder length-and-path generalization tests, including Edge Transformer memory limits (Figures 5 and 14–18). It also adds interval-algebra embedding analysis and revises the RCC-8 visualization. The original individual/combinatorial ablations and message-passing-depth study are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and 2-sigma errors over ten seeds for CLUTRR and three for RCC-8 and Graphlog. v2 explicitly extends the three-seed reporting statement to interval algebra; v1's interval-algebra table already contained uncertainties but lacked that explicit run count. This is additional disclosure, not evidence of increased runs.

E6.justification: Four Graphlog model scores are revised: World 6, for example, changes from 0.563 ± 0.016 to 0.648 ± 0.012 (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 2). v2 adds KGC results and efficiency/scaling outcomes, including reported accuracies of 0.74 on RCC-8 and 0.77 on interval algebra at 15 hops and 8 paths. CLUTRR and the component-ablation tables retain their scores.

T1.justification: The entailment lemmas, directional algebraic closure and expressivity proof already existed in v1's appendices; their promotion and renumbering are not new theory. v2 adds analytical parameter-count and runtime expressions in Section 4 and explicitly qualifies the closure/entailment correspondence for RCC-8 and interval algebra by requiring disjunction-free initial facts in Appendix C.

C1.justification: The central claim that epistemic inductive biases enable systematic GNN reasoning remains. v2 broadens the main contributions to competitiveness with specialized inductive KGC methods and explicitly claims at least two orders of magnitude fewer parameters than neuro-symbolic comparators. Both spatial and temporal benchmarks are now foregrounded, although both existed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 explains that its KGC setting need not require systematic generalization because training and test inference chains follow the same distribution. It also interprets shared semantic structure and identity relations in learned facets and qualifies when algebraic closure decides entailment. The original limitations concerning training artefacts and scarce data remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies KGC dataset statistics, a dataset-access reference, per-variant hyperparameters and inference formulas, plus interval-algebra settings and expanded hardware/runtime information (Appendix F). The original code/data repository was already disclosed. One new detail is inconsistent: Equation 20 uses argmax although the accompanying prose specifies minimizing cross-entropy.

R1.justification: The rewritten related-work section substantially broadens positioning around neuro-symbolic scalability, fuzzy and statistical relational frameworks, knowledge-graph models and systematic reasoning. New discussions include DeepProbLog, Logic Tensor Networks, lifted relational neural networks, R2N and LERP, alongside additional benchmark and tractability references.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, renames FB as EpiGNN, substantially rewrites the introduction and related work, and adds an explicit contribution list. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, existing interval-algebra material enters the main narrative, and the supplemental material is reorganized into Appendices A–G.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the separate RCC-8 and interval-algebra result tables with a combined six-panel plot, adds a spatial-relations illustration and KGC/efficiency/scaling displays, and relabels or redraws embedding heatmaps. Tables and surrounding text are also substantially rearranged in the conference layout; the main architecture schematic remains largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical validation: Table 3 tests applicability beyond the original reasoning benchmarks, while the efficiency comparisons and Appendix G.6 stress tests provide concrete support for previously largely qualitative scalability claims. Expanded experimental details and research positioning also improve the paper. These gains outweigh reporting drawbacks, including reduced numerical accessibility after replacing tables with plots, Equation 20's argmax/minimization inconsistency, and the blanket KGC order-of-magnitude parameter claim exceeding some ratios shown in Figure 14.
